title.rendered: Zacchaeus: Salvation Has Come to This House: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Today salvation has come to this house.” A morning devotional on the tax collector Jesus went home with.

content.rendered:
A short man climbed a sycamore tree in Jericho because he could not see over the crowd. Not just any short man. The chief tax collector of the region, wealthy from years of collaborating with Roman oppression, hated by his own people. When Jesus stopped under his tree and called him by name, the whole story of Zacchaeus turned around in one afternoon.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, September 11, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And Jesus said to him, ‘Today salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham; for the Son of Man has come to seek and to save that which was lost.'”
Luke 19:9-10 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Jericho, in the last few weeks of Jesus’ earthly ministry. He was on His way to Jerusalem for the Passover He would not survive. Crowds followed Him everywhere. And in the middle of the crowd that day was Zacchaeus. He was short, Luke tells us matter-of-factly. He was also the chief tax collector of Jericho, one of the wealthiest men in the region, and one of the most despised. Tax collectors worked for Rome. They gathered taxes from their own people and enriched themselves in the process. In the eyes of first-century Jews, Zacchaeus was a collaborator and a thief. And he wanted to see Jesus so badly that when the crowd blocked his view, he did the undignified thing. A rich, respectable-in-Rome businessman climbed a sycamore tree along the road and perched there like a schoolboy, just to catch a glimpse of the rabbi passing through.

Jesus stopped under the tree. Looked up. And said one of the most transforming sentences of His entire ministry. “Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for today I must stay at your house.” Not a lecture. Not a condemnation. Not a warning. An invitation to dinner. In the culture of the day, to eat at a person’s home was to publicly identify with them. Jesus was declaring, in front of the whole crowd, that He was choosing Zacchaeus. The tax collector. The traitor. The rich man everyone loved to hate. Zacchaeus scrambled down, joyful, and welcomed Jesus into his house.

The crowd complained. “He has gone to be a guest with a man who is a sinner.” But something was happening inside Zacchaeus that no one on the street could see. By the time dinner was over, Zacchaeus was on his feet, making a public declaration to the Lord. “Look, Lord, I give half of my goods to the poor; and if I have taken anything from anyone by false accusation, I restore fourfold.” Half of his wealth to the poor. And to anyone he had cheated, four times what he had taken. The mathematics of Old Testament restitution law required double repayment in most cases. Zacchaeus doubled that. He was not doing the minimum. He was doing what only a genuinely changed heart does. He was making right, generously and publicly, every wrong he could identify.

The Passion Translation captures the moment Jesus responded: “Then Jesus said, ‘This shows that today life has come to this household, and this man has been restored as a true son of Abraham. The Son of Man has come to seek out and to save those who are lost'” (Luke 19:9-10 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And Jesus said to him, Today is [Messianic and spiritual] salvation come to [all the members of] this household, since Zacchaeus too is a [real spiritual] son of Abraham; For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost” (Luke 19:9-10 AMPC). Salvation, that day, walked into the house of a man the whole town had written off.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the good news of Jesus in a single afternoon. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, no matter what your neighbours think of you, no matter what you have done in the past, no matter how many years you have collaborated with the wrong things, Jesus is still stopping under sycamore trees and calling short men down by name. He is still walking into houses the crowd has written off. He is still turning lives around in a single dinner. The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost. If you have been up a tree hoping just to catch a glimpse of Him, come down today. He is calling your name. He wants to come to your house.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus came to seek and to save the lost. He is not looking for the deserving. He is looking for the seeking, the curious, the hungry, the ones the crowd has written off. Today I come down from whatever tree I have been perched in. I welcome Jesus into my house. I welcome the salvation that walks in with Him. And wherever I need to make right the wrongs of my past, I ask You for the courage and generosity of Zacchaeus, to do it publicly, joyfully, and completely. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus has called me by name. Salvation has come to my house. The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost, and He found me. I welcome Him into every room today.
